Ophthalmology · published research

Conjunctival scar stenosis

In a 10-patient postoperative series, moderate wounds healed within two weeks and severe stenoses within three weeks after grafting, implantation, and LLLT. In rabbits, vascularization was higher at week four but the difference was absent at weeks six and eight.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

In a 10-patient postoperative series, moderate wounds healed within two weeks and severe stenoses within three weeks after grafting, implantation, and LLLT. In rabbits, vascularization was higher at week four but the difference was absent at weeks six and eight.

Summary of the Evidence

One unique 2021 publication combines an uncontrolled 10-patient postoperative series with a rabbit orbital-implant experiment. A later same-center report on contracted sockets concerns a similar graft-and-implant procedure; participant overlap cannot be ruled out, so it is not counted as independent confirmation. No standalone cell study was identified.

Human and clinical evidence

Xu and colleagues treated all patients with scleral graft transplantation, hydroxyapatite implantation, and postoperative low-level laser therapy. Moderate wounds reportedly healed within two weeks and severe stenoses within three weeks. There was no untreated or sham-treated human group, so the series cannot identify the contribution of laser or compare it with surgery alone (Xu et al. 2021).

Animal evidence

The same article included a rabbit model. Graft vascularization was greater in the PBM group at week four, but the difference was not present at weeks six or eight. This time-limited animal result is distinct from the uncontrolled human healing observations (Xu et al. 2021).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone in-vitro or ex-vivo experiment was identified. The rabbit observations are animal evidence, not a cell study.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The clinical protocol used 650 nm red laser at 3.8 J/cm², two or three times per week for one week; the rabbit protocol used five treatment days. These details apply to light used with graft surgery and an orbital implant. They do not establish an effect for PBM without surgery or for other socket procedures.

Interpretation

The publication reports postoperative healing and a temporary vascularization difference in rabbits. The lack of a human control and possible cohort overlap with the later report leave the clinical contribution of PBM uncertain.

Evidence strength in source summaryPostoperative healing after combined surgery and LLLT: Very low Rabbit graft vascularization: Very low

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

One publication combines a 10-patient uncontrolled postoperative series with a rabbit experiment. All human patients received grafting, implantation, and LLLT, so there is no untreated clinical comparison. A later same-center contracted-socket study may overlap and is not independent confirmation. Controlled human replication is needed.
